The system ::: the system ::: substantive ::: Working definition adopted in this deep-dive series. :::  ::: All the services around a person — health, housing, social care, justice, substance use, domestic abuse and welfare, whether statutory, commissioned or voluntary-sector — seen from the person's point of view rather than any one agency's. The related principle is that the system should adapt to the person, not the person to the system. :::  ::: The system

Trauma-aware / -curious / -informed / -responsive ::: TRAUMA-AWARE ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Changing Futures programme — the local trauma-informed maturity framework (four developmental phases). :::  ::: The four developmental phases in the South Tees framework. An organisation is trauma-responsive when Trauma-informed practice (TIP) is the norm and no longer dependent on champions. Trauma-Informed Champion ::: champion|TIP champion|Trauma-Informed Champion ::: local-programme ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures). :::  ::: A trained practitioner who has committed, via the Trauma-Informed Champions Charter, to embedding trauma-informed practice within their employing organisation. South Tees identified 67 named champions across 11 services. :::  ::: Trauma-Informed Champion
Trauma-Informed Champions Charter ::: Charter|Champions Charter ::: local-programme ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures). :::  ::: South Tees's local commitment to trauma-informed practice, funded through Changing Futures. It asks every service to recognise the impact of trauma and respond with kindness and compassion, built on six principles: safety; trust and transparency; choice and voice; collaboration; empowerment; and inclusivity. :::  ::: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter
Trauma-informed practice (TIP) ::: trauma-informed practice|TIP ::: substantive ::: OHID (2022) Working definition of trauma-informed practice (GOV.UK) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/working-definition-of-trauma-informed-practice/working-definition-of-trauma-informed-practice) :::  ::: A whole-system approach to realising the prevalence of trauma, recognising its effects, responding by embedding that knowledge in practice, and resisting re-traumatisation. The series adopts the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) (2022) England working definition, with Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)'s (2014) four assumptions and six principles as the underlying framework. ::: TIP ::: Trauma-informed practice

Workstream ::: workstream ::: local-programme ::: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2); STCFP Board Terms of Reference. :::  ::: One of the strands the programme is organised into. The Delivery Plan sets out six: a governance strand (Programme Management and Ideas Factory) and five delivery strands — Enhanced Case Management, Innovation Fund, Key Worker Support, VCS Infrastructure, and Embedding Trauma-Informed Services. Workstreams are how the programme delivers, as distinct from the five areas of complex need that define who it works with. :::  ::: Workstream
